observations: External view of a window air conditioner with the front panel removed.
Visible internal components include a large cooling coil, compressor, and electrical wiring.
The unit is sitting on a blue and grey tiled floor in what appears to be a warehouse or storage area.
The unit is not plugged in or running; it is shown as a static scrap item.
No brand name, model number, or technical specifications are visible on the unit.

claims.evidence: No rating plate or technical specification sticker is visible in the photo.
The unit is shown with its casing removed and internal components exposed, which is typical for scrap or parts.
The design, including the external grille and internal coil, is characteristic of a window-mounted unit.

risks.risk: The unit may not be functional or may have internal electrical faults.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit plugged in and successfully cooling a room.

risks.risk: The cooling coil may be clogged with dust or frost, preventing heat exchange.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the coil with a magnifying glass or a thermometer showing a significant drop in temperature.
risks.if_unproven: as having a non-functional cooling system

risks.risk: The compressor may be seized or leaking refrigerant.
risks.proof: A video of the unit running with a thermometer showing a drop in temperature.

risks.risk: The unit may be a counterfeit or a different brand from the seller's description.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's rating plate (usually on the back or inside).

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the rating plate (usually on the back or inside) to confirm the brand and model.
Video of the unit plugged in and running.
Photo of the cooling coil with a thermometer to check for frost.
Photo of the compressor area to check for leaks.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
